title: U.S. House · Maryland's 4th District
area: Most of Prince George's County, including Bowie, Upper Marlboro and part of Waldorf.

context.text: Incumbent Glenn Ivey defeated Joseph Gomes, Shavonne Hedgepeth, Jakeya Johnson and Jonathan White in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. George McDermott ran unopposed in the Republican primary. Sam Husseini qualified for the Green Party line.

summary.text: Glenn Ivey is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 4th Congressional District. A lawyer and former federal prosecutor, he chaired the Maryland Public Service Commission and served two terms as Prince George's County State's Attorney before his 2022 election to Congress. He is seeking a third term.

background.text: Born in Chelsea, Massachusetts, in 1961. According to his congressional website, he grew up in Rocky Mount, North Carolina, and Dale City, Virginia.
Graduated from Princeton University in 1983 (B.A. in politics) and Harvard Law School in 1986.

Began his legal career in the litigation department of the Baltimore firm Gordon, Feinblatt, Rothman, Hoffberger & Hollander, and served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia from 1990 to 1994.

Worked on Capitol Hill as a legislative assistant to Rep. John Conyers, counsel to the Senate Whitewater Committee for Sen. Paul Sarbanes, and chief counsel to Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle. He was later a partner at Preston, Gates, Ellis and at Venable, and taught as an adjunct law professor at the University of Maryland (1995-2014) and Harvard (2013-2021).
Appointed chairman of the Maryland Public Service Commission by Gov. Parris Glendening in 1998.

Elected State's Attorney for Prince George's County in 2002 and served two consecutive terms; his congressional website cites a Domestic Violence Prosecution Unit and a mortgage fraud unit created during his tenure.
Elected to Congress in 2022 and sworn in in January 2023. Served on the Judiciary and Homeland Security Committees in the 118th Congress and now serves on the Appropriations and Ethics Committees.

Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 79.2% of the vote. According to his congressional website, he lives in Prince George's County with his wife, Jolene, a county councilmember, and has six children.

priorities.text: Gun safety, saying Congress should stand up to groups that oppose common regulation of firearms.

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website says there should be universal background checks and a federal license to purchase a firearm, more ATF funding, accountability for the gun industry, and a renewed ban on military-style assault weapons.
His 2022 campaign website says Congress must codify safe access to reproductive health and urges passage of the Women's Health Protection Act.
positions.quote: Congress must act to codify safe access to reproductive health.

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website says he supports restructuring the tax system so the wealthiest Americans and big corporations pay their fair share.
positions.quote: restructuring the tax system so that the wealthiest Americans and big corporations pay their fair share

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website says he supports increasing the minimum wage to a livable wage.
positions.quote: I support increasing the minimum wage to a livable wage

positions.summary: His 2022 campaign website says he would work to create green energy jobs by moving the country away from dependence on fossil fuels.
positions.quote: moving us away from our dependence on fossil fuels

record.text: Serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Commerce-Justice-Science and Financial Services subcommittees) and House Ethics Committee for the 2025-2026 term.
Served on the House Homeland Security and Judiciary Committees during the 2023-2024 term.

candidates.name: George McDermott

summary.text: George McDermott is the Republican nominee for Maryland's 4th Congressional District. He has worked as a victim rights advocate and has run for this seat several times, in the Democratic primary in 2012 and as the Republican nominee in 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2024.

background.text: Earned a trade school diploma, according to Ballotpedia, and has worked as a victim rights advocate.
Ran in the 2012 Democratic primary for the 4th District, losing to incumbent Donna Edwards (5.1% to her 91.8%), and in the 2014 Republican primary, losing to Nancy Hoyt.
Won the 2016 Republican primary and lost the general election to Anthony Brown; ran again as the Republican nominee in 2018 (19.9%) and 2020 (20.2%), losing to Brown both times.
Was the Republican nominee in 2024, losing to Glenn Ivey, 88.4% to 11.2%.
Advanced from the June 23, 2026 Republican primary as the only candidate on the ballot, receiving 1,923 votes.

priorities.text: Holding the executive, legislative and judicial branches accountable to the Constitution, per his Mission statement.

Judicial accountability: his campaign Q&A page, which includes a 2018 Red Maryland survey, gives as top priority legislation requiring leaders to inform the public about secret matters and holding the judiciary to its canons of conduct.

positions.summary: In a March 2024 Baltimore Sun interview, says Congress should protect the right to choose after Dobbs.
positions.quote: As a candidate victim’s rights advocate, father, and believer in a woman’s right to choose.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website read. Answers on guns, taxes and welfare there do not address the guide statements directly; the Q&A page and survey are undated or from 2018. The Baltimore Sun 2024 interview (via Ballotpedia) is the source of the abortion position; his Gaza answer is too garbled in that transcription to quote. No 2026 questionnaire found.

candidates.name: Sam Husseini

summary.text: Sam Husseini is the Green Party nominee for Maryland's 4th Congressional District. Describes himself as an independent journalist who has spent about 25 years at the Institute for Public Accuracy.

background.text: Attended the Bronx High School of Science and earned a bachelor's degree from Carnegie Mellon University in 1987.

According to his Ballotpedia survey response, he worked for a year at Moody's Investors Service after graduating, then as a computer programmer, helped manage a homeless shelter, and was a substitute teacher in public schools.

Describes working at the media watch group FAIR and the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee, and for the last 25 years at the Institute for Public Accuracy, where he says he has drafted thousands of news releases.
Describes himself as an independent journalist and says he has lived in the 4th District for over 20 years.

priorities.text: Peace and a foreign policy based on law: ends U.S. funding of Israel and reduces military spending.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page calls for ending all U.S. funding to Israel.
positions.quote: Stop genocide of Palestinians in Gaza, all funding to apartheid Israel

positions.summary: Campaign issues page lists Medicare for All.
Campaign issues page calls for raising taxes on the rich and closing loopholes, including on corporate taxes.
positions.quote: Dramatically increase it on the rich, closing manipulative loopholes -- including with corporate taxes and financial transaction tax.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page calls for abolishing ICE.
positions.quote: Ensure civil liberties. Stop and abolish ICE
